TAPI v.2.4.0/2.4.1

The following table describes the Generic service settings for "ConnectivityService" and "ConnectivityServiceEndPoint" properties used by the T-API.

Property Type Description Example

"ConnectivityService"

name

Array

Items NameValue

Navigator MC support is limited to a single element that contains service label.

 
"name": [
	{
      "value-name": "label",
      "value": "CDC-MRSNC-27-postman"
    }
  ]

layer-protocol-name

String

Specificies the T-API service layer. Which can be one of PHOTONIC_MEDIA, DIGITAL_OTN, DSR or ETH MCP 4.0 supports:
1. PHOTONIC_MEDIA which maps to Navigator MC photonic services
2. DIGITAL_OTN which maps to Navigator MC L1 ODU services
3. DSR which maps to Navigator MC L1 rates other than ODU
4. ETH which maps to Navigator MC L2 services

 
"layer-protocol-name": "PHOTONIC_MEDIA"

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:bit-rate

Integer

Specifies the bit-rate for ODU Flex Service which is in bits/second rate. Valid values include: 1249177230, 2498354460, 3747531690, 4996708920, 6245886150, 7495063380, 8744240610, 9993417841, 11290233185, 12544703539, 13799173893, 15053644247, 16308114601, 17562584955, 18817055309, 20071525663, 21325996017, 22580466371, 23834936724, 25089407078, 26343877432, 27598347786, 28852818140, 30107288494, 31361758848, 32616229202, 33870699556, 35125169910, 36379640264, 37634110618, 38888580972, 40143051325, 42948415395, 44249882528, 45551349661, 46852816795, 48154283928, 49455751061, 50757218194, 52058685327, 53360152460, 54661619594, 55963086727, 57264553860, 58566020993, 59867488126, 61168955259, 62470422393, 63771889526, 65073356659, 66374823792, 67676290925, 68977758059, 70279225192, 71580692325, 72882159458, 74183626591, 75485093724, 76786560858, 79389495124, 78088027991, 80690962257, 81992429390, 83293896524, 84595363657, 85896830790, 87198297923, 88499765056, 89801232189, 91102699323, 92404166456, 93705633589, 95007100722, 96308567855, 97610034989, 98911502122, 100212969255, 101514436388, 102815903521, 104117370654, 1244160000, 2498775126, 10037273924, 40319218983, 104794445815

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:bit-rate": 2498354460

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:trib-slot

Integer

Specifies the tribslots for ODU Flex Service. Valid values range from 1 to 80

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:trib-slots": 2

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:line-rate

String

Specifies the lineRate for ODU Flex Service. Valid values are - ODUFLEX, ODU0, ODU1, ODU2, ODU2e, ODU3 and ODU4

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:line-rate": "ODUFLEX"

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:service-type

String

Specifies the service type for Layer 2 Service. Valid values are - EVPL and EPL

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:service-type": "EVPL"

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:oam-enabled

Boolean

Specifies the boolean value for oam-enable at the service level for Layer 2 Service. Valid values are - true and false

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:oam-enabled": true

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ccm-interval

String

Specifies the interval for the ccm at the service level for Layer 2 Service.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ccm-interval": "1sec"

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ma-name

String

Specifies the ma name for Layer 2 Service.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ma-name": "tapi_lldp"

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ccm-priority

Integer

Specifies the priority of the ccm for Layer 2 Service. Valid values are - 0 to 7

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ccm-priority": 3

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:linear-only

Boolean

Specifies the boolean value to support port constraints for Layer 2 Service.

In case we need to provide the port topology constraints (include-node-edge-point/exclude-node-edge-point), we need to set the "linear-only" attribute, so that Navigator MC considers only Ethernet links & LAG for route computation. 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:linear-only": true

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:core-svid

Integer

Specifies the core svid value at the service layer for Layer 2 Service. Valid values are : 1 to 4094

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:core-svid" : 4090

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:tunnel-directionality

String

Specifies the constraint for directionality for the tunnel for Layer 2 Service. Valid values are - unidirectional and bidirectional

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:tunnel-directionality":"bidirectional"

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:spur-allowed

Boolean

Specifies the boolean value for AllowQinQSpur for Layer 2 Service.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:spur-allowed":true

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:transport-protection

String

Specifies the transport-protection level for Layer 2 Service. Valid values are - "PROTECTED_BEST_EFFORT", "PROTECTED_ONLY", "UNPROTECTED_BEST_EFFORT", "UNPROTECTED_ONLY"

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:transport-protection":"PROTECTED_ONLY"

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protected-pseudowire

Boolean

Specifies the boolean value for pseudowire protection for Layer 2 Service.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protected-pseudowire":true

topology-constraint.exclude-node-edge-point

Array Items: String

Constrains routing with a list of node-edge-points to be excluded when routing the service. NodeEdgePoints are specified as T-API nep UUIDs.

 
"topology-constraint": [{exclude-node-edge-point": "b22445cc-0f3e-3d42-a4db-96a221438275"}]

topology-constraint.include-node-edge-point

Array Items: String

Constrains routing with a list of node-edge-points to be included when routing the service. NodeEdgePoints are specified as T-API nep UUIDs.

 
"topology-constraint": [{include-node-edge-point": "45b0f5e1-4302-3328-8802-d22557834010"}]

end-point

Array Items: ConnectivityServiceEndPoint

The list of service endpoints

See table below.

resilience-type

Object: Members: restoration-policy:String protection-type:String

The type of resiliency (protection/restoration). The protection-type member specifies the requested resilience type. Values can be one of the following: NO_PROTECTON, NO_PROTECTION, ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION, ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_DYNAMIC_RESTORATION, ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_MANUAL_RESTORATION, MANUAL_RESTORATION or DYNAMIC_RESTORATION:

  • NO_PROTECTON is used for un-protected photonic services and layer 1 unprotected p-snc services using TAPI version 2.1.3 and lower.

  • NO_PROTECTION is used for un-protected photonic services and layer 1 unprotected p-snc services using TAPI version 2.4.0 or later.

  • DYNAMIC_RESTORATION is used for MR photonic services and s-snc layer 1 services.

  • ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION is used for protected layer 1 services with p-snc.

  • ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_DYNAMIC_RESTORATION is used for protected layer 1 services with s-snc.

  • ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_MANUAL_RESTORATION is used when either the current or protection route is impaired (e.g. by a failure or maintenance command), the pre-computed route is implemented to restore resiliency level..

  • MANUAL_RESTORATION is used when restoration scheme where the protection route is pre-computed. When the current (and only) route is impaired (e.g. by a failure or maintenance command) the pre-computed route is implemented.

Restoration-policy member is not used and is ignored if supplied. 
"resilience-type":{"protection-type": "DYNAMIC_RESTORATION"}

preferred-restoration-layer

String

Specificies the T-API service layer. Which can be one of PHOTONIC_MEDIA, DIGITAL_OTN.

MCP 7.0+ supports:
1. PHOTONIC_MEDIA which maps to Navigator MC photonic services
2. DIGITAL_OTN which maps to Navigator MC L1 ODU services
 
"preferred-restoration-layer": "DIGITAL_OTN"

reversion-mode

String

The reversion-mode specifies the requested reversion mode. Values can be one of the following: REVERTIVE, NON-REVERTIVE, or NON_REVERTIVE:

  • NON_REVERTIVE/NON-REVERTIVE is used when a Connection switched to a lower priority (non-preferred/spare/protection) resource will not revert to a higher priority (preferred/intended/nominal) resource when that recovers. This mode is typically applied when there is no ranking between the redundant resources.

  • REVERTIVE is used when a Connection switched to a lower priority (non-preferred/spare/protection) resource will revert to a higher priority (preferred/intended/nominal) resource when that recovers (potentially after some wait-to-restore time).

 
"reversion-mode": "REVERTIVE"

resilience-constraint

Object:
Members:
reversion-mode: String
wait-to-revert-time: ValueUnit

It Specifies resilience-constraints for editing SNCP PU parameters :- Specifies the requested mode of restoration of the service.
reversion-mode can be:

  • REVERTIVE

  • NON-REVERTIVE

  • NON_REVERTIVE

wait-to-revert-time can be:
If the protection/restoration scheme is revertive, this attribute specifies the time, in minutes, to wait after a fault clears on a higher priority (preferred) resource before reverting to the preferred resource.

 
"resilience-constraint":{"reversion-mode":"REVERTIVE","wait-to-revert-time":480}

tapi-path-computation:exclude-node

Array Items: String

Constrains routing with a list of nodes to be excluded when routing the service. Nodes are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-path-computation:exclude-node": ["f344643b-0be9-3e5e-8e52-81fc4bb85509"]

tapi-path-computation:include-node

Array Items: String

Constrains routing with a list of nodes to be included when routing the service. Nodes are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
""tapi-path-computation:include-node": ["f6f45f17-5e9f-32f2-a3d7-258bf68e670c"],"]

requested-capacity

Object:
Members:
total-size: ValueUnit
otu-rate: String

Specifies the requested capacity of the service. Both Integer and String values are accepted for capacity. It is recommended to use Integer value as per the TAPI standard.

Allowed values for otu-rate are:

  • OTUC1

  • OTUC2

  • OTUC3

  • OTUC4

  • OTUC5

  • OTUC6

  • OTUC7

  • OTUC8

 
"requested-capacity": {"total-size": {"value": 300,"unit": "GBPS" }}

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:capacity-extensions

Object:
Members:
baudRate: String
isForMultipleRoutes: Boolean

Specifies the capacity extensions of the service.
baudRate can be:

  • 35GBAUD.

  • 56GBAUD.

  • 95GBAUD.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:capacity-extensions": {"isForMultipleRoutes": false,"baudRate": "35GBAUD" }

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:osrp-enabled

Boolean

Specifies whether osrp is enabled for the service.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:osrp-enabled": true

cost-characteristic

Array of Object:
Members:
cost-name: String
cost-value: String

Specifies cost constraints to be applied during service routing
- max-latency, primary-max-latency: Specify max latency for primary route in microseconds
- min-latency, primary-min-latency: Specify min latency for primary route in microseconds
- minimize-latency: Specifies that routing should minimize latency
- admin-weight: Specifies max admin weight for primary route
- restoration-max-latency: Specify max latency for restoration route in microseconds
- restoration-min-latency: Specify min latency for restoration route in microseconds
- restoration-minimize-latency: Specifies that routing should minimize latency for restoration path
- restoration-admin-weight: Specifies max admin weight for primary route

The same list of cost characteristics are supported for protection path, by prefixing “protect” to the cost-name, e.g. “protect-max-latency”

 
"cost-characteristic": [
    {
        "cost-name": "admin-weight",
        "cost-value": "1000"
    },
    {
        "cost-name": "restoration-max-latency",
        "cost-value": "2000"
    },
    {
        "cost-name": "protect-max-latency",
        "cost-value": "2000"
    },
    {
        "cost-name": "protect-restoration-max-latency",
        "cost-value": "2000"
    }
]

"ConnectivityServiceEndPoint"

name

Array Items NameValue

Navigator MC support is limited to a single element containing an endpoint location in the following form:

node:<node name>-shelf:<shelf>-slot:<slot>-port:<port>

 
name”: [{“value-name”: “location”, “value”: “node:PV0728CRFE-shelf:1-slot:26-port:1”}],

service-interface-point

Object

The uuid of the T-API service interface point (SIP).

A request can use either the name property or the service-interface-point property to specify the requested service port. If both are specified, the name property is ignored.

 
“service-interface-point": {service-interface-point-uuid”: “8132aa4a-9887-3364-94bf-11766050a1ea”}

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:endpoint-type

String

Specifies the endpoint type for the endpoints for Layer 2 Service. Valid values are - "A_UNI", "Z_UNI", "Z_PRIME_UNI", "UNI", "ENNI", "A_ENNI", "Z_ENNI", "Z_PRIME_ENNI", "INNI"

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:endpoint-type": "Z_UNI"

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ingress-ether-type

String

Specifies the String value for the possible ether types at the endpoint level for Layer 2 Service. Possible values include "8100", "88A8" and "9100".

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ingress-ether-type": "8100"

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:untagged-data-vid

Integer

Specifies the integer value for untagged vids at the endpoint level for Layer 2 Service in case the vid is untagged(4096). Possible values include integers from 1 to 4094.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:untagged-data-vid": 40

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:oam-enabled

Boolean

Specifies the boolean value for oam-enable at the endpoint level for Layer 2 Service.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:oam-enabled": true

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ccm-transmit-enabled

boolean

Specifies the boolean value to enable the ccm-transmit at the endpoint level for Layer 2 Service.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ccm-transmit-enabled": true

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:vid

Array Items:Integer

Specifies the array of integer containing possible vid values for the endpoints for Layer 2 Service. Valid values are : 0 to 4097

We only support values 0 to 4094 for EVPL services. In order to provision only untagged service, VID should be specified as 4096. In order to provision catch-all service, VID should be specified as [4096,4097]. Also, there is no support for defining the VLAN range e.g. [100-110] in TAPI requests. Only comma-separated values are supported e.g. [101,102,103,104,105,106,107,108,109,110] 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:vid":[101,102]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:cir

Integer

Specifies the cir value in kbps for in case of a policied Layer 2 Service.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:cir": 200000

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ebs

Integer

Specifies the ebs value in kbytes for in case of a policied Layer 2 Service.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ebs": 400

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:cbs

Integer

Specifies the cbs value in kbytes for in case of a policied Layer 2 Service.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:cbs": 600

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:eir

Integer

Specifies the eir value in kbps for in case of a policied Layer 2 Service.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:eir": 40000

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protection-type

String

Specifies the type of protection for an OTN Optical Service. Valid values are: APS and SNCP.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protection-type": "SNCP"

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protection-starts-at

String

Specifies where the protection starts for OTN Optical Service. Valid values are: AT_THE_ENDPOINT, AT_THE_FIRST_OPPORTUNITY and ON_A_DEVICE_WITH_CENTRAL_FABRIC.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protection-starts-at": "AT_THE_FIRST_OPPORTUNITY"

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:signal-conditioning

String

Specifies the laser status for the endpoint. Only applies to broadband endpoints or switching endpoints (full rate). Valid values are: LASERSHUTOFF,NONE and NA.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:signal-conditioning": "LASERSHUTOFF"

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ains

String

Specifies whether the endpoint should automatically be put in-service. Only applies to broadband endpoints or switching endpoints (full rate). Valid values are: ACTIVE and INACTIVE.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:ains": "ACTIVE"

layer-protocol-qualifier

String

Specifies the requested service layer. Values can be one of the following:
“ODU_TYPE_ODU2”, ”ODU_TYPE_ODU2e”, ”ODU_TYPE_ODU4”, ”ODU_TYPE_ODU3”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_10_GigE_WAN”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_40_GigE”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_100_GigE”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_400_GigE”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_192”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_64”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_768”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_256”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_GigE”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_48”,"DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_12", "DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_3", “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_16”, "DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_1", "DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_4", “ODU_TYPE_ODU1”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_100”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_200”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_400”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_800”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_1200”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_1600”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_3200”, “FICON1G”, “FICONEXPRESS2G”, “FICON4G”, “FICON8G”,“FICON16G”, or “PHOTONIC_LAYER_QUALIFIER_OTSi”

Navigator MC does not support asymmetric service creation, and the specified layer-protocol-qualifier must be the same for both endpoints in the service.

 
"layer-protocol-qualifier": "ODU_TYPE_ODU1"

Photonic service restorable settings

The following table details the T-API values necessary to create a restorable photonic service. The settings are additions and constraints to the generic service settings specified in the following table.

TAPI v2.1.3 / v2.4.0/2.4.1
Property Type Description Example

"ConnectivityService" Settings for Photonic Service Restorable

service-layer

String

Must be set to PHOTONIC_MEDIA

 
"service-layer": "PHOTONIC_MEDIA"

resilience-type

Object: Members: protection-type:String

protection-type must be set to DYNAMIC_RESTORATION

 
"resilience-type":{"protection-type": "DYNAMIC_RESTORATION}

spectral-assign-option

String

Specifies the spectral assignment option and can be one of the following: SPECTRUM_SPREAD, PACK_LOW, PACK_HIGH

center-frequency

Number

Specifies the requested center frequency. If specified, this overrides the spectral-assign-option.

maximize-capacity

Boolean

Maximize capacity for a single photonic service

preferred-restoration-layer

String

May be specified as one of the following values: "PHOTONIC_MEDIA".

"preferred-restoration-layer": "PHOTONIC_MEDIA"

diversity-exclusion

Array Items: String

UUIDs of T-API Connections to be used as diversity exclusions.

 
“diversity-exclusion": ["f6f45f17-5e9f-32f2-a3d7-258bf68e670c"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-exclude-node

Array Items: String

Constrains the restoration path with a list of nodes to be excluded when routing the service. Nodes are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-exclude-node": ["f344643b-0be9-3e5e-8e52-81fc4bb85509"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-include-node

Array Items:String

Constrains the restoration path with a list of nodes to be included when routing the service. Nodes are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-include-node": ["f6f45f17-5e9f-32f2-a3d7-258bf68e670c"],

include-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the primary path with a list of links (OMS) to be included when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"include-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

exclude-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the primary path with a list of links (OMS) to be excluded when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"exclude-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-include-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the restoration path with a list of links (OMS) to be included when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-include-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-exclude-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the restoration path with a list of links (OMS) to be excluded when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-exclude-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

restoration-path-diversity-exclusions

Array Items: String

UUIDs of T-API Connections to be used as diversity exclusions for the restoration path.

 
“restoration-path-diversity-exclusion": ["f6f45f17-5e9f-32f2-a3d7-258bf68e670c"]

ConnectivityServiceEndpoint Settings for Photonic Service Restorable

layer-protocol-qualifier

string

Must be set to “PHOTONIC_LAYER_QUALIFIER_OTSi”

 
"layer-protocol-qualifier": "PHOTONIC_LAYER_QUALIFIER_OTSi"

String

UUID of T-API Service Interface Point (SIP), it allows for the specification of the CMD port on the photonic NE

Note:

  • Ideally central-frequency should be specified at endpoint level i.e. "otsia-connectivity-service-end-point-spec". However for backward compatibility, it can be specified at Connectivity-Service level also as "tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:center-frequency". If both are specified, then priority would be given to "otsia-connectivity-service-end-point-spec" central-frequency. If mentioned at end-point level, value should be same for both end-points.

  • grid-type is a conditional parameter in TAPI 2.4.0 and later i.e. It will not be reported when not mapped in Navigator MC.

Example of a High Capacity Photonic Service Request on mated configurations

Photonic Service provisioning on mated configurations is the same as regular service creation. If adjacencies between CMD and transponder ports have been fully configured for the mated configuration, then only the SIPs representing the OTN service endpoints need to be present in the request. If however adjacencies have not been configured, it is required to specify the CMD sips via the photonic-interface-point extension to the endpoint property in the request. In this case, both the primary and mate ports need to be included as shown in the example below.

{
    "layer-protocol-name" : "PHOTONIC_MEDIA",
    "end-point" : [
        {
            "service-interface-point" : {"service-interface-point-uuid" : "362d1581-11ad-3ad8-a4d6-3049c4c10341"},
            "photonic-interface-point": { "service-interface-point-uuid": "1a9432f1-1753-3132-bfce-5d6ce4297577" },
            "layer-protocol-qualifier" : "tapi-photonic-media:PHOTONIC_LAYER_QUALIFIER_OTSi"
        },
        {
            "service-interface-point" : {
            "service-interface-point-uuid" : "b9099282-9307-355b-8b87-b74ad7e0cb91"
            },
            "photonic-interface-point": { "service-interface-point-uuid": "e5defbab-540e-3eab-b860-fae01698ae41" },
            "layer-protocol-qualifier" : "tapi-photonic-media:PHOTONIC_LAYER_QUALIFIER_OTSi"
        },
        {
            "service-interface-point" : {
            "service-interface-point-uuid" : "b782b63d-9424-3308-854a-24a37ccea78c"
            },
            "photonic-interface-point": { "service-interface-point-uuid": "e620434e-1371-3ca2-b759-e234fe0b5d9c" },
            "layer-protocol-qualifier" : "tapi-photonic-media:PHOTONIC_LAYER_QUALIFIER_OTSi"
        },
        {
            "service-interface-point" : {
            "service-interface-point-uuid" : "856c7d67-2052-3f38-a236-56f40466932e"
            },
            "photonic-interface-point": { "service-interface-point-uuid": "a1cec7d5-5959-3e3a-a86e-c1de7ad1e20a" },
            "layer-protocol-qualifier" : "tapi-photonic-media:PHOTONIC_LAYER_QUALIFIER_OTSi"
        }
    ],
    "requested-capacity" : {
        "otu-rate" : "OTUC8",
        "total-size" : {
            "unit" : "GBPS",
            "value" : "800"
        }
    },
    "tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:capacity-extensions" : {
        "baud-rate": "95GBAUD"
    },
    "tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:maximize-capacity" : false,
    "name" : [
        {
            "value-name" : "label",
            "value" : "TAPI WS MATED 2"
        }
    ],
    "osrp-enabled": true,
    "tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:spectral-assign-option": "CENTER_OUTWARDS"
}

The following Navigator MC options are not supported, or indicate the limitations in T-API:

  • Service scheduling: The provisioning time is always "now".

  • SNC and SNC label: The SNC is created with only a default label.

  • Service Bundling: This attribute always defaults to “auto-assign service bundle” with a default label.

  • The following routing constraints apply:

    • “Compute best route”

TAPI v2.4.0/2.4.1
Property Type Description Example

"ConnectivityService" Settings for Photonic Service Restorable

layer-protocol-name

String

Must be set to PHOTONIC_MEDIA

 
"layer-protocol-name": "PHOTONIC_MEDIA"

resilience-type

Object: Members: protection-type:String

protection-type must be set to DYNAMIC_RESTORATION

 
"resilience-type":{"protection-type": "DYNAMIC_RESTORATION}

spectral-assign-option

String

Specifies the spectral assignment option and can be one of the following: SPECTRUM_SPREAD, PACK_LOW, PACK_HIGH

center-frequency

Number

Specifies the requested center frequency. If specified, this overrides the spectral-assign-option.

maximize-capacity

Boolean

Maximize capacity for a single photonic service

preferred-restoration-layer

String

May be specified as one of the following values: "PHOTONIC_MEDIA".

"preferred-restoration-layer": "PHOTONIC_MEDIA"

diversity-exclusion

Array Items: String

UUIDs of T-API Connections to be used as diversity exclusions.

 
“diversity-exclusion": ["f6f45f17-5e9f-32f2-a3d7-258bf68e670c"]

include-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the primary path with a list of links (OMS) to be included when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"include-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

exclude-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the primary path with a list of links (OMS) to be excluded when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"exclude-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

restoration-path-diversity-exclusions

Array Items: String

UUIDs of T-API Connections to be used as diversity exclusions for the restoration path.

 
“restoration-path-diversity-exclusion": ["f6f45f17-5e9f-32f2-a3d7-258bf68e670c"]

ConnectivityServiceEndpoint Settings for Photonic Service Restorable

layer-protocol-qualifier

string

Must be set to “PHOTONIC_LAYER_QUALIFIER_OTSiMC”

 
"layer-protocol-qualifier": "PHOTONIC_LAYER_QUALIFIER_OTSiMC"

photonic-interface-point

String

UUID of T-API Service Interface Point (SIP), it allows for the specification of the CMD port on the photonic NE

 
“photonic-interface-point”: {"service-interface-point-uuid": “27ea607e-f757-34b4-98cf-bc67759740b8”}

otsia-connectivity-service-end-point-spec

Object

The central-frequency member of otsia-connectivity-service-end-point-spec specifies the central frequency in Hz.

 
"otsia-connectivity-service-end-point-spec": { "otsi-config": [{ "central-frequency": { "central-frequency": 193200000000000 } } ] }

resilience-constraint.resilience-route-constraint

List of Object

The resilience-route-constraint can be used to be specify topology constraints for restoration, protecting and restoration-proctecting paths. The local-id is used to identity the path and can be one of "protecting-path", "restoration-path" or "protecting-restoration-path"

 
"resilience-constraint": {"resiliency-route-constraint": [{"local-id": "restoration-path","topology-constraint": {"include-link": [{"topology-uuid": "4e537278-79f8-39ad-804b-f0b553cb2ffb","link-uuid": "2779cdcb-4cce-306d-989d-0969a5de88d3"}]]}}]}

Transport client service non-switched settings

The following table details the T-API values necessary to create a non-switched transport client service. The settings are additions or constraints to the generic service settings specified in the following table.

TAPI v2.1.3
Property Type Description Example

"ConnectivityService" Settings for non-switched Transport Client

service-layer

String

Must be set to ODU or DSR.

 
"service-layer": "ODU"

resilience-type

Object: Members: protection-type:String

The value of "protection-type" must be set to NO_PROTECTION, or the resilience-type can be left out of the request.

 
"resilience-type":{"protection-type": "NO_PROTECTION}

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:service-type-constraint

String

Directs Navigator MC to choose the specific service type. Possible values are: INCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE, EXCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE

Must be set to EXCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE

 
“tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:service-type-constraint”: “EXCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE”

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:diversity-type

String

The value of "diversity-type" must be set to NONE or LINK_DIVERSE. The diversity-type can be left out of the request for no diversity or can be set NONE value.

 
“tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:diversity-type”: “LINK_DIVERSE”

connectivity-constraint

Object

Connectivity constraint have following properties: diversity-exclusion, requested-capacity, restoration-path-diversity-exclusion.

See table below(ConnectivityConstraint).

ConnectivityServiceEndpoint Settings for non-switched Transport Client

layer-protocol-qualifier

string

Must be set to one of the following values:
”ODU_TYPE_ODU2”, ”ODU_TYPE_ODU2e”, ”ODU_TYPE_ODU4”, ”ODU_TYPE_ODU3”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_10_GigE_WAN”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_40_GigE”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_100_GigE”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_400_GigE”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_192”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_64”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_768”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_256”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_GigE”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_48”, "DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_12", "DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_3", “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_16”, "DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_1", "DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_4", “ODU_TYPE_ODU1”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_100”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_200”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_400”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_800”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_1200”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_1600”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_3200”, “FICON1G”, “FICONEXPRESS2G”, “FICON4G”, “FICON8G”, “FICON16G”

 
"layer-protocol-qualifier": "ODU_TYPE_ODU1”

ConnectivityConstraint Settings for non-switched Transport Client

diversity-exclusion

Array Items: Object Member: connectivity-service-uuid: String

UUIDs of T-API connectivity-service to be used as diversity exclusions. It is applicable only when diversityType have some value other than NONE.

 
"diversity-exclusion":[{"connectivity-service-uuid": "11aa1bf0-78fe-11ec-ae85-0509d30f169b"}]

Transport client non-switched with automatic line service creation

ONF TAPI TR-547 specifications assumes that in cases where there is no multiplicity and no flexibility, a DSR request can drive the creation of a server line service. This feature is supported for selected set of broadband cards in MCP 7.2.

Line services created as part of client service request, will automatically be removed, when the client service is deleted, if no other client service is dependent on the line service. The line service will be a separate ConnectivityService in TAPI.

Current support includes

  1. WL5e card NTK540BC

  2. WL5e card NTK540BD

  3. WL5e card NTK540CD

  4. WLAi card NTK538DR

  5. WLAi card NTK538FR

The selection of line service photonic ports and line service capacity is automatic based on the client service request. These values can however also be explicitly controlled by the TAPI client via the ConnectivityService extensions listed in the table below. These extensions apply to both TAPI 2.1.3 and TAPI 2.4.0/2.4.1 .

Property Type Description Example

"ConnectivityService" Settings for non-switched Transport Client

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:preferred-line-capacity

Object:
Members:
total-size: ValueUnit
otu-rate: String
baud-rate: String

Specifies the requested capacity of the supporting line service. Both Integer and String values are accepted for capacity. It is recommended to use Integer value as per the TAPI standard.

Allowed values for otu-rate are:

  • OTUC1

  • OTUC2

  • OTUC3

  • OTUC4

  • OTUC5

  • OTUC6

  • OTUC7

  • OTUC8

Allowed values for baud-rate are:

  • 35GBAUD.

  • 56GBAUD.

  • 95GBAUD.

  • 31P5GBAUD.

 
"requested-capacity": {"total-size": {"value": 300,"unit": "GBPS" }}

"ConnectivityService Endpoint" Settings for non-switched Transport Client

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:preferred-supporting-line-port

String

UUID of T-API Service Interface Point (SIP), allowing for explicit selection of supporting line port. The SIP must be the photonic port from which the line service will originate

 
“tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:preferred-supporting-line-port”: {"service-interface-point-uuid": “27ea607e-f757-34b4-98cf-bc67759740b8”}

Example of a non switched Transport Client with explicit selection of line capacity and line ports

{
	"name": [{
		"value-name": "SERVICE_NAME",
		"value": "100GE-client-2"
	}],
	"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:service-type-constraint": "EXCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE",
	"end-point": [{
			"service-interface-point": {
				"service-interface-point-uuid": "551f8f1a-7157-3f58-a149-90420cad5d00"
			},
			"layer-protocol-qualifier": "tapi-dsr:DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_100_GigE",
			"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:preferred-supporting-line-port": {
				"service-interface-point-uuid": "908d2d6f-a64c-3dcb-8e04-c1a9aa6eac5c"
			}
		},
		{
			"service-interface-point": {
				"service-interface-point-uuid": "f834ad35-91bb-357f-9795-88138811dbf8"
			},
			"layer-protocol-qualifier": "tapi-dsr:DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_100_GigE",
			"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:preferred-supporting-line-port": {
				"service-interface-point-uuid": "d5e96076-80e5-3908-87bb-31339d4a9432"
			}
		}
	],
	"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:preferred-line-capacity": {
		"total-size": {
			"value": 800,
			"unit": "GBPS"
		},
		"baud-rate": "95GBAUD",
		"otu-rate": "OTUC8",
		"transcoding": "Ethernet"
	},
	"layer-protocol-name": "DSR",
	"layer-protocol-qualifier": "tapi-dsr:DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_100_GigE"

Transport client service switched (control-plane) settings

The following table details the T-API values necessary to create a switched transport client service. The settings are additions or constraints to the generic service settings specified in the following table.

TAPI v2.1.3
Property Type Description Example

"ConnectivityService" Settings for switched Transport Client

service-layer

String

Must be set to ODU or DSR.

 
"service-layer": "ODU""

resilience-type

Object: Members: protection-type:String

The value of "protection-type" must be set to NO_PROTECTION or DYNAMIC_RESTORATION.

If "protection-type" is set to NO_PROTECTION, Navigator MC creates a service with P-SNC.

If "protection-type" is set to DYNAMIC_RESTORATION, Navigator MC creates a service MR-SNCs.

 
 "resilience-type":{"protection-type": "DYNAMIC_RESTORATION”}

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:service-type-constraint

String

Directs Navigator MC to choose the specific service type. Possible values are: INCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE, EXCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE

Must be set to INCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE.

 
“tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:service-type-constraint”: “INCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE”

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-exclude-node

Array Items: String

Constrains the restoration path with a list of nodes to be excluded when routing the service. Nodes are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-exclude-node": ["f344643b-0be9-3e5e-8e52-81fc4bb85509"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-include-node

Array Items: String

Constrains the restoration path with a list of nodes to be included when routing the service. Nodes are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-include-node": ["f6f45f17-5e9f-32f2-a3d7-258bf68e670c"],

include-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the primary path with a list of links (ODU) to be included when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API Link UUIDs.

 
"include-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

exclude-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the primary path with a list of links (ODU) to be excluded when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API Link UUIDs.

 
"exclude-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-include-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the restoration path with a list of links (ODU) to be included when routing the service. Links are specified as Link node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-include-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-exclude-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the restoration path with a list of links (ODU) to be excluded when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-exclude-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:diversity-type

String

Must be set to one of the following values: "NONE", "LINK_DIVERSE", "BUNDLE_DIVERSE", "NODE_DIVERSE", "NODE_BUNDLE_DIVERSE". The diversity-type can be left out of the request for no diversity or can be set NONE value.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:diversity-type":"LINK_DIVERSE"

connectivity-constraint

Object

Connectivity constraint have following properties: diversity-exclusion, requested-capacity, restoration-path-diversity-exclusion.

String

The following Navigator MC options are not supported or indicate the limitations in T-API:

  • Service scheduling - Provisioning is always now

  • Routing constraints - Applies to both home and restoration paths:

    • Compute best route

Transport client service switched protected (control-plane) settings

The following table details the T-API values necessary to create a protected switched transport client service. The settings are additions or constraints to the generic service settings specified in the following table.

TAPI v2.1.3
Property Type Description Example

"ConnectivityService" Settings for switched Transport Client*

service-layer

String

Must be set to ODU or DSR.

 
"service-layer": "ODU"

resilience-type

Object: Members: protection-type:String

The value of "protection-type" must be set to: ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION or ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_DYNAMIC_RESTORATION

If "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION, Navigator MC creates a service with P-SNC on both the home path and restoration path.

If "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_ DYNAMIC_RESTORATION, Navigator MC creates a service with MR-SNC on both home and restoration paths.

 
"resilience-type":{"protection-type": " ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION”}

route-exclusivity

String

The value of "route-exclusivity" can be one of the following: Working, WorkingProtect and Preferred

If "protection-type" is set to NO_PROTECTION, only Working and Preferred can be specified.

If "protection-type" is set to DYNAMIC_RESTORATION, all 3 values can be specified.

If "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION, only Working can be specified.

If "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_ DYNAMIC_RESTORATION, both Working and WorkingProtect can be specified.

 
"route-exclusivity": "Working"

protect-route-exclusivity

String

Applicable only when "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION or ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_ DYNAMIC_RESTORATION. The value of "protect-route-exclusivity" can be one of the following: Working and WorkingProtect

If "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION, only Working can be specified.

If "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_ DYNAMIC_RESTORATION, both Working and WorkingProtect can be specified.

 
"protect-route-exclusivity": "WorkingProtect"

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:service-type-constraint

String

Directs Navigator MC to choose the specific service type. Possible values are: INCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE, EXCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE

 
“tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:service-type-constraint”: “INCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE”

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-exclude-node

Array Items: String

Constrains the restoration path with a list of nodes to be excluded when routing the service. Nodes are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-exclude-node": ["f344643b-0be9-3e5e-8e52-81fc4bb85509"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-include-node

Array Items:String

Constrains the restoration path with a list of nodes to be included when routing the service. Nodes are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-include-node": ["f6f45f17-5e9f-32f2-a3d7-258bf68e670c"],

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-exclude-node

Array Items: String

Constrains the protection home path with a list of nodes to be excluded when routing the service. Nodes are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-exclude-node": ["f344643b-0be9-3e5e-8e52-81fc4bb85509"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-include-node

Array Items:String

Constrains the protection path with a list of nodes to be included when routing the service. Nodes are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-include-node": ["f6f45f17-5e9f-32f2-a3d7-258bf68e670c"],

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-restoration-path-exclude-node

Array Items: String

Constrains the protection restoration path with a list of nodes to be excluded when routing the service. Nodes are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-restoration-path-exclude-node": ["f344643b-0be9-3e5e-8e52-81fc4bb85509"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-restoration-path-include-node

Array Items:String

Constrains the protection restoration path with a list of nodes to be included when routing the service. Nodes are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-restoration-path-include-node": ["f6f45f17-5e9f-32f2-a3d7-258bf68e670c"]

include-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the primary path with a list of links (ODU) to be included when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API Link UUIDs.

 
"include-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

exclude-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the primary path with a list of links (ODU) to be excluded when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API Link UUIDs.

 
"exclude-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-include-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the restoration path with a list of links (ODU) to be included when routing the service. Links are specified as Link node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-include-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-exclude-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the restoration path with a list of links (ODU) to be excluded when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:restoration-path-exclude-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-include-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the protection primary path with a list of links (ODU) to be included when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API Link UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-include-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-exclude-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the protection primary path with a list of links (ODU) to be excluded when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API Link UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-exclude-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-restoration-path-include-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the protection restoration path with a list of links (ODU) to be included when routing the service. Links are specified as Link node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-restoration-path-include-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-restoration-path-exclude-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the protection restoration path with a list of links (ODU) to be excluded when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API node UUIDs.

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:protecting-restoration-path-exclude-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:diversity-type

String

Must be set to one of the following values: "LINK_DIVERSE", "BUNDLE_DIVERSE".

 
"tapi-ciena-connectivity-service-extensions:diversity-type":"LINK_DIVERSE"

preferred-restoration-layer

String

May be specified as one of the following values: "ODU".

"preferred-restoration-layer": "ODU"

ConnectivityServiceEndpoint Settings for protected switched Transport Client

layer-protocol-qualifier

String

Must be set to one of the following values:
“ODU_TYPE_ODU2”, ”ODU_TYPE_ODU2e”, ”ODU_TYPE_ODU4”, ”ODU_TYPE_ODU3”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_10_GigE_WAN”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_40_GigE”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_100_GigE”, ”DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_192”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_64”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_768”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_256”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_GigE”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_48”, "DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_12", "DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_OC_3", “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_16”, "DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_1", "DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_STM_4",“ODU_TYPE_ODU1”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_100”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_200”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_400”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_800”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_1200”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_1600”, “DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_FC_3200”, “FICON1G”, “FICONEXPRESS2G”, “FICON4G”, “FICON8G”, “FICON16G”.

 
"layer-protocol-qualifier": "ODU_TYPE_ODU1”

odu-connectivity-service-end-point-spec

Object

This object consists of 3 member objects (Optional).

1. oduCsepCommonPac

opuTributarySlotSize :- This attribute is applicable for ODU2 and ODU3 CTP only. It indicates the slot size of the ODU CTP.

oduRate :- This attribute indicates the rate of the ODU termination point in Kbits/s. The default value is derived from the configured n of the ODUCn as defined in Table 7-2/G.709 v5.

numberOfOduC:- This attribute specifies the number of ODUC instances of the ODUCn.

oduType:- This attribute specifies the type of the ODU termination point.

2. oduCsepCtpPac

tributarySlotList:- This attribute contains a set of distinct (i.e. unique) integers (e.g. 2, 3, 5, 9, 15 representing the tributary slots TS#2, TS#3, TS#5, TS#9 and TS#15) which represents the resources occupied by the ODUk CTP (e.g. an ODUflex with a bit rate of 6.25G setup over an HO-ODUk).

tributaryPortNumber:- This attribute identifies the tributary port number that is associated with the ODUk CTP. This attribute applies when the ODUk CTP is multiplexed into a server layer ODU TTP object.

3. oduCsepTtpPac

configuredMappingType :- This attribute indicates the configured mapping type.

configuredClientType :- This attribute configures the type of the client CTP of the server ODU TTP.

customMappingType :- This attribute indicates the proprietary attribute to specify the Navigator MC-only mappings for configuredMappingType

 
"odu-connectivity-service-end-point-spec":{"odu-csep-ttp-pac":{"configured-client-type":"DIGITAL_SIGNAL_TYPE_10_GigE_WAN","configured-mapping-type":"GFP-F"}}

TAPI v2.4.0/2.4.1
Property Type Description Example

"ConnectivityService" Settings for switched Transport Client*

layer-protocol-name

String

Must be set to DIGITAL_OTN or DSR

 
"layer-protocol-name": "DIGITAL_OTN"

resilience-type

Object: Members: protection-type:String

The value of "protection-type" must be set to: ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION or ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_DYNAMIC_RESTORATION

If "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION, Navigator MC creates a service with P-SNC on both the home path and restoration path.

If "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_ DYNAMIC_RESTORATION, Navigator MC creates a service with MR-SNC on both home and restoration paths.

 
"resilience-type":{"protection-type": " ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION”}

route-exclusivity

String

The value of "route-exclusivity" can be one of the following: Working, WorkingProtect and Preferred

If "protection-type" is set to NO_PROTECTION, only Working and Preferred can be specified.

If "protection-type" is set to DYNAMIC_RESTORATION, all 3 values can be specified.

If "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION, only Working can be specified.

If "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_ DYNAMIC_RESTORATION, both Working and WorkingProtect can be specified.

 
"route-exclusivity": "Working"

protect-route-exclusivity

String

Applicable only when "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION or ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_ DYNAMIC_RESTORATION. The value of "protect-route-exclusivity" can be one of the following: Working and WorkingProtect

If "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION, only Working can be specified.

If "protection-type" is set to ONE_PLUS_ONE_PROTECTION_WITH_ DYNAMIC_RESTORATION, both Working and WorkingProtect can be specified.

 
"protect-route-exclusivity": "WorkingProtect"

String

Directs Navigator MC to choose the specific service type. Possible values are: INCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE, EXCLUDES_CONTROL_PLANE_CORE

include-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the primary path with a list of links (ODU) to be included when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API Link UUIDs.

 
"include-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

exclude-link

Array Items:String

Constrains the primary path with a list of links (ODU) to be excluded when routing the service. Links are specified as T-API Link UUIDs.

 
"exclude-link": ["d81b7242-40e5-3dce-8869-845fc0ca3407"]

resilience-constraint.resilience-route-constraint

List of Object

The resilience-route-constraint can be used to be specify topology constraints for restoration, protecting and restoration-proctecting paths. The local-id is used to identity the path and can be one of "protecting-path", "restoration-path" or "protecting-restoration-path"

 
"resilience-constraint": {"resiliency-route-constraint": [{"local-id": "restoration-path","topology-constraint": {"include-link": [{"topology-uuid": "4e537278-79f8-39ad-804b-f0b553cb2ffb","link-uuid": "2779cdcb-4cce-306d-989d-0969a5de88d3"}]]}}]}

Asymmetric DSR Service Creation

ONF TAPI TR-547 allows for situations, where a service may be initiated in one domain and handed over to another network domain managed by a different TAPI server. This implies service creation between UNI and E-NNI SIPs, where the UNI CSEP refers to a DSR SIP and the NNI CSEP refers to a DIGITAL_OTN SIP. Navigator MC TAPI supports this as asymmetric service creation between DSR UNI and OTUk E-NNI interfaces.

Current support includes

  1. 1GE UNI to ODU0 NNI

  2. 10GE UNI to ODU2e NNI

  3. 10GE UNI to ODU2 NNI

  4. 40GE UNI to ODU3 NNI

  5. 100GE UNI to ODU4 NNI

  6. OC3/12, STM1/4 UNI to ODU0 NNI

  7. OC48, STM16 UNI to ODU1 NNI

  8. OC192, STM64 UNI to ODU2 NNI

Layer 0 / Layer 1 T-API service deletion

To delete a service created via T-API or Navigator MC UI, complete these steps:

  1. Retrieve the UUID of service to be deleted via GET:

    /tapi/data/tapi-common:context/tapi-connectivity:connectivity-context/connectivity-service/

  2. Send T-API service deletion request DELETE:

    /tapi/data/tapi-common:context/tapi-connectivity:connectivity-context/connectivity-service={connectivity-service-uuid}

Layer 0 / Layer 1 Edit of Service Label

Navigator MC TAPI supports editing of the Service Label associated with a L0 or L1 ConnectivityService. The editing of the ConnectivityService label is reflected to the TAPI Connection implementing the ConnectivityService.

The editing of the label is supported via a POST operation on the name component of the ConnectivityService.

By default There is no check for a duplicate named Layer-0 service created on same NE by TAPI. To enable this the ifd config property ifd.l0.requireUniqueIntentLabel has to be set true. Use the market API to update this value if required. To retrieve and update resources, use the Market API as described below.

  1. Retrieve the Resource ID from the Resource body by executing the following request.

    Specify resourceTypeId = ifd.v6.resourceTypes.IfdConfig

    Sample request:

    GET {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

    The response body includes the following:

    "id": "5f296487-d9f6-4f84-9719-9eae341fe602"

  1. Patch the resource.

    Specify the resourceId = 5f296487-d9f6-4f84-9719-9eae341fe602

    Sample request:

    PATCH {NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{resourceId}

    {
    "properties": {
        "configurationProperties": {
            "ifd.l0.requireUniqueIntentLabel": {
                "value": "true"
            }
        }
    }
}

    Sample response:

    OK
For photonic services SNCs are not mapped to TAPI ConnectivityService. Label edit is therefore only supported for the photonic services and not the underlying L0 SNCs
Property Type Description Example

name

Array of Name, Value pairs

The name property is an array of Name, Value pairs. For ConnectivityService instances Navigator MC TAPI supports a single element in the array, where the element name is "label"

{ "value-name": "label", "value": "NewServiceLabel" }
Example Request and Response

Edit ConnectivityService label .

Payload data (application/json)

{
"value-name": "label",
"value": "NewServiceLabel"
}

Response

{
"uuid": "5cf81b12-03c4-4e0d-ac4b-57036c176db7",
"name": [{
    "value-name": "label",
    "value": "NewServiceLabel"
    }
]
}

Layer 0 / Layer 1 and Layer T-API promotion of Service Level Connection

Discovered L0 and L1 service level Connections can be promoted to managed services represented as TAPI ConnectivityService Instances. This is done by posting a ConnectivityService which is constrained to adopt the existing connection.

This will cause the creation of a ConnectivityService instance matching the promoted Connection.

Please note that the Navigator MC TAPI does not support promoting and editing properties in a single operation. If a Connection is being promoted in order to edit the properties of the Connection, then the editing needs to be performed in a subsequent operation.

Property Type Description Example

connection-inclusion

Array of String

List the uuids of the connections to be adopted by the ConnectivityService instance. Currently Navigator MC supports listing a single top level connection representing a discovered service level connection

{ "connection-inclusion": ["03d4e420-dd09-326c-88c1-26897ceacfd0"] }

Promote discovered Connection.

Payload data (application/json)

{
"connection-inclusion": ["03d4e420-dd09-326c-88c1-26897ceacfd0"]
}

Response

{
"uuid": "5cf81b12-03c4-4e0d-ac4b-57036c176db7"
}

T-API objects deep discovery and notifications support via BulkSync API.

The following section highlights the details on how T-API objects are discovered and sent as notifications using the Bulk Sync API interface.

Starting MCP 4.0, the L0/L1 T-API discovery module publishes into the respective kafka topics in addition to persisting the following objects in ElasticSearch.

L0/L1/L2 T-API Objects

The following are T-API Objects:

  • Node

  • Link

  • NodeEdgePoint

  • Connection

  • ConnectionEndPoint

  • ConnectivityService

  • ServiceInterfacePoint

  • Device

  • Equipment

  • EquipmentHolder

Layer 0 / Layer 1 / Layer 2 T-API bulksync websocket URLs

Requirements

Before you start, ensure the following:

  • A valid Navigator MC authentication token must be provided in the header of the websocket connection request - "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

  • Uni-directional "Pong" frame is required periodically in order to keep an idle websocket connection open.

  • Usage of "start_from" query param to resume a stream using the stream token, or begin from the current point in time using keyword "Latest".

  • If a stale stream token is specified, which would place the user in a compacted portion of the websocket stream, a special "HEAD" message will be sent indicating that the user’s stream has been reset to the beginning. All existing data should be purged or audited as some deletes or updates may be missed. The new incoming stream will provide a full view of the current network.

Solution (Bulk Resync and Notification)

Bulk Resync is a reactive streaming API service that works with a kafka back end. The service streams out kafka data using a websocket protocol. At a high level, it aims to achieve following:

  • Guarantees at least once delivery on API streaming.

  • Supports websocket protocol.

  • Clients can consume messages from beginning of time.

  • Clients can suspend and resume from any previously known token.

  • Clients can only monitor latest messages.

  • Supports reactive-streaming backpressure.

  • Supports Boolean expression filters on messages.

Bulk Resync Architecture

Bulk Resync architecture is based off Akka reactive-streaming library. It uses Alpakka library (i.e., built on top of Akka streams) for communication with kafka. Each websocket/SSE connection is independently maintained by separate pipeline, which ensures and guarantees the e2e message delivery, fail-over, and back-pressure. It does not keep any cache in the memory except client state during the connection, and the whole pipeline gets shutdown on client disconnect.

Key problems and solutions in Bulk Resync/Notifications:

  1. Fast producer and slow consumer

    In this scenario, particularly when external clients (websocket or SSE) connects via kafka-mediation layer, the clients do not have any control in terms of the way the data is consumed from the mediation server. It is quite common that when external clients are set to read out from large kafka datasets (in millions) from set of topics, the mediation layer streaming server should guarantee to emit the data only if there is a demand from the clients. Otherwise, this would lead to fast producer and slow consumer problems, which ultimately can cause the data loss at the client side, unless it has been handled using back-pressure protocol. Akka streams is used according to its Akka documentation.

    The back pressure protocol is defined in terms of the number of elements a downstream subscriber that is able to receive and buffer. This is referred as demand. The source of data (referred to as Publisher in Reactive Streams terminology and implemented as Source in Akka Streams) guarantees that it will never emit more elements than the received total demand for any given subscriber.

    In this case, back-pressuring the Publisher is required, because the subscriber is not able to cope with the rate at which its upstream (streaming server) would like to emit data elements.

  2. At least once Guarantee delivery

    As a general practice, when using kafka consumer instead of relying on the consumer lib to commit the offset periodically, you can take the control to manually commit the offset when you know the record is really consumed. When you do this using manual offset control, it is guaranteed that you read the record once. However in failure cases, you could receive duplicate records. The actual consumer (websocket or sse clients in our example) lives outside of the kafka consumer process. In such case, it does not give us exact control when the message is actually consumed, unless the client sends an ack on every message it consumes, or the client stores/manages the offset remotely.

    The solution is not to assume whether the message is consumed or not. Instead, give the control to end clients to resume from the given token any time.

    Basically, the token is a base64 encoded string that represents a location across given topic/partition/offsets mapping. This means, at server side, for every message or at every Nth message, you send a token along with original message to the client.

    GroupId Topic Partition* Offset Current Position Client Token

    A

    T1

    0

    1

    [(T1, 0, 1), (T1, 1, 2), (T2, 0, 0)]

    abcd123=

    A

    T1

    0

    2

    [(T1, 0, 2), (T1, 1, 2), (T2, 0, 0)]

    abcd124=

    A

    T1

    0

    3

    [(T1, 0, 3), (T1, 1, 2), (T2, 0, 0)]

    abcd125=

    A

    T1

    1

    [(T1, 0, 3), (T1, 1, 2), (T2, 0, 0)]

    abcd126=

    A

    5

    [(T1, 0, 3), (T1, 1, 5), (T2, 0, 0)]

    pqrs125=

    A

    T2

    0

    0

    [(T1, 0, 3), (T1, 1, 5), (T2, 0, 0)]

    pqrs125=
Websocket IDLE connections

In order to support long-running websocket connections and backpressure scenario, the client is expected to send uni-directional Pong frame (https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6455#section-5.5.3), in which case a response from the server is not expected.

These Pong frames are necessary to keep idle connections from being closed. They also ensure that the connection remains usable even after no data frames are communicated over a longer period of time.

BulkSync Message Schema

Example, BulkSync Message

T-API Bulk Streaming API usage/examples

Authentication:

WebSocket request should include Authorization: Bearer <authtoken> header OR cookie header uac.authorization=<authtoken>

Available streams for Layer 0 / Layer 1 / Layer 2 T-API bulksync websocket:

(1) Client can asks for list of supported stream types using
GET https://<host>/tapi/data/context/stream-context/supported-stream-type

Example below shows response with node and link stream type and its log configuration details.

[
    {
        "stream-type-id": "d6d95fac-e46e-30a5-9469-aa033e11b7f8",
        "stream-type-name": "node-stream",
        "stream-type-content": [
            "OBJECT_CLASS_IDENTIFIER_NODE"
        ],
        "record-retention-period": "1 day",
        "segment-size": "1GB",
        "log-storage-strategy": "COMPACTED",
        "log-record-strategy": "WHOLE_ENTITY_ON_CHANGE"
    },
    {
        "stream-type-id": "37c2b5f1-0f70-3104-bbab-d4a67a5e2a9c",
        "stream-type-name": "link-stream",
        "stream-type-content": [
            "OBJECT_CLASS_IDENTIFIER_LINK"
        ],
        "record-retention-period": "1 day",
        "segment-size": "1GB",
        "log-storage-strategy": "COMPACTED",
        "log-record-strategy": "WHOLE_ENTITY_ON_CHANGE"
    }
]

(2) Client asks for list of available streams using
GET https://<host>/tapi/data/context/stream-context/available-stream/

Sample response looks as below

[
    {
        "stream-id": "b1453347-09ef-33f3-a05f-723bf7eea14f",
        "stream-state": "STREAM_STATE_ACTIVE",
        "stream-connection-type": "d6d95fac-e46e-30a5-9469-aa033e11b7f8",
        "connection-protocol": "websocket",
        "connection-address": "wss://<host>/tapi/data/context/stream-context/available-stream=b1453347-09ef-33f3-a05f-723bf7eea14f"
    },
    {
        "stream-id": "a3a612b7-5732-3e00-ac9a-aedfcf367a8b",
        "stream-state": "STREAM_STATE_ACTIVE",
        "stream-connection-type": "37c2b5f1-0f70-3104-bbab-d4a67a5e2a9c",
        "connection-protocol": "websocket",

    }
]

(3) Using the connection-address URL listed in step 2 client can establish the websocket connection from the client.

How to resume the stream by specifying token?

wss://<host>/tapi/data/context/stream-context/available-stream=a3a612b7-5732-3e00-ac9a-aedfcf367a8b/?start_from=abcd125=

How to consume the latest stream starting from Time = now?

wss://<host>/tapi/data/context/stream-context/available-stream=a3a612b7-5732-3e00-ac9a-aedfcf367a8b/?start_from=latest

SNC Home Notifications

Starting in MCP 4.2, the "mcp-view" microservice supports publishing the SNC on/off home path and home available status using a BulkSync websocket API endpoint.

When a client connects to the API endpoint, it will receive the SNC change-events for the following cases:

  • off-home-path SNCs returning to on-home-path

  • on-home-path SNCs switching to off-home-path

  • SNCs home-available status changes from true to false

  • SNCs home-available status changes from false to true

The change-events for off/on home path and home available status will be published for the following SNC domain types:

  • L0 MR-SNC

  • L1/OTN MR-SNC

  • L1/OTN MR-SNCP

  • L1/OTN NMR-SNC

  • L1/OTN NMR-SNCP

Websocket API Endpoint

GET wss://<NAVIGATOR_MC_HOST>/mcpview/api/v1/fre/change-events/snc/?start_from=latest

WebSocket request should include Authorization: Bearer <authtoken> header OR cookie header uac.authorization=<authtoken>

Off Home Path Event Example

{
"header": {
    "token": "ZGr3:1575183165190_0:2024412249:AAAAAQAAAJY=",
    "key": "-1695434707069579216-snc::controlPlane",
    "message_type": "EVENT",
    "internal": {
        "partition": 0,
        "offset": 22
    }
},
"version": "BULKSYNC/1.0",
"body": {
    "version":"1",
    "event_type":"ResourceSnapshot",
    "object_type":"com.ciena.bp.view.SncOnHomeStatus",
    "object_id":"-1695434707069579216-snc::controlPlane",
    "object_data": {
        "onHome":false
    }
}
}

On Home Path Event Example

{
"header": {
    "token": "ZGr3:1575183165190_0:2024412249:AAAAAQAAAJA=",
    "key": "-1695434707069579216-snc::controlPlane",

        "partition": 0,

    }
},

    "version":"1",

    "object_id":"com.ciena.bp.view.SncOnHomeStatus",

        "onHome":true
    }
}
}

Home Available Event Example

{

    "token": "ZGr3:1575183165191_0:2024412249:AAAAAQAAAJB=",

Provision L1 NCP unprotected service through REST API

You can use the Navigator MC API to provision an unprotected transport client service for the below supported rate.

List of Supported Rates: 1 GbE, 1 Gbe ODUFlex, 10 GbE, 25 GbE, 100 GbE, OC3, OC12, OC48, OC192, ODU0, ODU1, ODU2, ODU2e, ODU4, STM1, STM4, STM16, STM64

Prerequisites

  • Local and remote network elements should be synced successfully in Navigator MC.

  • Line modules (and pluggable, if applicable) supporting connection endpoints must be provisioned on the network element.

  • You should be familiar with the following TOSCA definitions:

    • L1NCPServiceIntent.tosca

    • ServiceIntent.tosca

    • L1NCPClientServiceIntentFacade.tosca

    • L1NCPServiceIntentFacadeBase.tosca

    • L1NCPClientServiceIntentFacadeTemplate.tosca

Steps

  1. Authorize and connect to the Navigator MC server.

    Description: This command will connect to Navigator MC and generate a bearer token to be used for consecutive commands. The value of the token retrieved above will go in header of all subsequent request against the key “Authorization”.

    POST {BP_SERVER}/tron/api/v2/tokens

    Request Parameters in Body:

    Key Value

    grant_type

    password

    username

    <user name of Navigator MC user>

    password

    <password of Navigator MC user>

  1. Request Commit route for L1 NCP SNC service

    Description: Commit route store tpe and fre expectation of L1 NCP SNC service in NSI.

    POST - {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{INTENT_RSC_ID}/operations*

    POST - {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/5f1940f4-1ddd-462c-a92f-03263737308b/operations*

Step 5 request route data passes in commit route request service for NCP SNC.

Sample request:

{
  "interface": "commitRoute",
  "inputs": {
    "routes": [
      {{SELECTED_ROUTE}}
    ],
    "routes_equipment":[
    ]
  }
}

Provision L1 NCP SNCP protected service through REST API

NCP SNCP protection supports in below two way:-

  • NCP SNCP protected connection without tail

    • This type of connection will be having core SNCP only and tail will not be present in both source and destination endpoint.

    • Pure switching connection of this type can be having only switching card(PKTOTN, USSM) in both endpoint and core. In Pure switching connection broadband card can not be used.

    • Broadband card like TRM NTK532GA and NTK532GN also supports NCP SNCP protected connection without tail.

    • Macro client service structures:

      • (client) switched OTN node - zero or more switched OTN nodes - switched OTN node (client)

      • (client) switched OTN node - mix of broadband fiber switch ("patch") nodes and zero or more switched OTN nodes - switched OTN node (client)

    • This type of connection supports fully terminated and fully unterminated (ODUk or Channelized) services

  • NCP SNCP protected connection with tail

    • User should be able to provision symmetric SNCP protected non-control plane client services originating and/or terminating on broadband tails.

    • This type of connection supports fully terminated and fully unterminated (ODUk or Channelized at the same rate as the end to end service) services

    • Macro structures (Core can contain patch nodes)

      • (client) Tail - SNCP protected core - Tail (client)

      • (client) SNCP protected core - Tail (client)

      • (client) Tail - SNCP protected core (client)

Both NCP SNCP connection with and without tail supports in 6500 S-series and T-Series

  • Both NCP SNCP connection with and without tail supported rates:

    • OTUk, k = 1, 2, 2e, 4

    • ETHn, n = 1G, 10G, 100G

    • STM-n, n= 1, 4, 16, 64

    • OCn, n= 3, 12, 48, 192

NCP APS 1+1 protected connection

  • User can provision NCP APS 1+1 by selecting APS option as shown in below image by selecting APS option in 'End Type' dropdown and selecting At the endpoint option in 'Protection' dropdown

  • NCP APS 1+1 supported rates:

    • ETH10G

    • STM-64

    • OC192

    • FC800, FC1200

    • FICON8G

  • For protection in NCP two new drop down 'End Type' and 'Protection' has been added in MCP 5.0 under "Transport client - Protected" option. User can select protection type from drop down for provisioning SNCP or APS service. Below subsequent two screenshot describe about protection type and protection required for both endpoint in Navigator MC GUI.

  • User has to select 'protection' option from drop down on the basis of NCP SNCP connection configuration whether NCP SNCP connection has tail in either or both endpoint or SNCP core is starting or ending with the cards like PKTOTN, TRM NTK532GA, TRM NTK532GN. As shown in the below screenshot it has three following options 'At the endpoint', 'At the first opportunity' and 'On a device with central fabric'.

  • User can choose different Protection type and required option for endpoints, following are the protection schemes for various configuration types like PKTOTN, TRM NTK532GA and TRM NTK532GN:

    Tail—​TRM NTK532GA←-Work/Protect-→PKTOTN

Prerequisites

Before you begin:

  • Local and remote network elements should be synced successfully in Navigator MC.

  • Line modules (and pluggable, if applicable) supporting connection endpoints must be provisioned on the network element.

  • You should be familiar with the following TOSCA definitions:

    • L1NCPServiceIntent.tosca

    • ServiceIntent.tosca

    • L1NCPProtServiceIntent.tosca

    • L1NCPProtClientServiceIntentFacade.tosca

    • L1NCPProtClientServiceIntentFacadeTemplate.tosca

Steps

  1. Authorize and connect to the Navigator MC server.

    Description: This command will connect to Navigator MC and generate a bearer token to be used for consecutive commands. The value of the token retrieved above will go in header of all subsequent request against the key “Authorization”.

    POST {BP_SERVER}/tron/api/v2/tokens

    Request Parameters in Body:

    Key Value

    grant_type

    password

    username

    <user name of Navigator MC user>

    password

    <password of Navigator MC user>

    Sample response:

  {
    "token": "91535cbcf2b72f606efd",
    "user": "f55b7423-2729-4c2c-890e-e86ebd503ee6",
    "loginDetail": {
      "time": "2020-07-21T06:25:49Z",
      "ipAddress": "172.16.0.1",
      "userAgent": "PostmanRuntime/7.9.1",
      "sessionId": "fde7fa83-5113-4a23-befa-b50807393f4f",
      "sessionType": "Machine"
    },
    "createdTime": "2020-07-21T06:25:49Z",
    "inactiveExpirationTime": null,
    "isSuccessful": true,
    "timeout": 2592000,
    "userTenantUuid": "b5f76246-80e8-4f7d-8457-f265ce9bb8e0",
    "radiusState": "",
    "failedLoginAttempts": 0,
    "lastSuccessIpAddress": "172.16.0.1",
    "lastSuccessLogin": "2020-07-21 06:25:49+00:00",
    "postLoginMessage": null
  }

  1. Retrieve product id from Navigator MC Server

    Description: Different service types are mapped to different products in Navigator MC. This step is to retrieve the product id of the type of the service (NCP SNCP) the user wants to create. In this case, it is L1NCPProtClientServiceIntentFacade.

    GET {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/products?includeInactive=false&q=resourceTypeId%3Aifd.v6.resourceTypes.L1NCPProtClientServiceIntentFacade&limit=1000

    Sample response:

  {
     "id": "5f165694-3f73-4a05-bd29-66a7e2f3cb8d",
     "resourceTypeId": "ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L1NCPProtClientServiceIntentFacade",
     "title": "product for ifd.v6.resourceTypes.L1NCPProtClientServiceIntentFacade",
     "active": true,
     "domainId": "built-in",
     "constraints": {},
     "providerData": {
       "template": "ifd.v6.serviceTemplates.L1NCPProtClientServiceIntentFacade"
     }
   },

  1. Create facade for L1 NCP SNCP Protection service

    Description: The facade encapsulates all request parameters provided by user. Whenever an external client connects to Navigator MC Server, it needs to send in all request parameter in facade used for that service. In this case, it is L1NCPProtClientServiceIntentFacade.

    POST {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources

    Request Parameters:

    Parameter Value

    product ID

    Retrieved from step 2

    Label or name

    <name of the SNCP>

    interactive_mode

    True/False

    Layer rate

    <layer rate>

    Ex: DSR_10GE, OC192, ODU0, ODU2 etc

    endpoint A

    • <Network Element> name A end

    • Shelf A end

    • Slot A end

    • Port A end

    • ChannelizedEndPointInfo A-End (for OTN)

      • tribPort

      • payloadType

      • layerRate

      • tribSlot

    endpoint Z

    • NE name Z end

    • Shelf Z end

    • Slot Z end

    • Port Z end

    • ChannelizedEndPointInfo Z-End (for OTN)

      • tribPort

      • payloadType

      • layerRate

      • tribSlot

    protection type

    • value

    • string ['SNCP', 'APS']

    protection starts at

    • value

    • string ['AT_ENDPOINT', 'AT_FIRST_OPPORTUNITY', 'ON_CENTRAL_FABRIC']

    sourceProtectionUnitController

    • autoReversionPossible <boolean value>

    • autoReversionType <delay, timeOfDay> <Refer to the table below>

    • timerGuard

    • timerDetectionGuard

    • timerRecoveryGuard

    destinationProtectionUnitController

    • autoReversionPossible <boolean value>

    • autoReversionType <delay, timeOfDay> <Refer to the table below>

    • timerGuard

    • timerDetectionGuard

    • timerRecoveryGuard

    work path constraint

    • value

    • objectType (OTU_LINKS_NAME)

    • constraintType (HARD)

    protect path constraint

    • value

    • objectType (OTU_LINKS_NAME)

    • constraintType (HARD)
    The values of attribute protectionType is APS and protectionStartsAt is AT_THE_ENDPOINT for APS1+1 connection.
    The values of attribute autoReversionType are applicable when the value of protectionStartsAt attribute is ON_CENTRAL_FABRIC for SNCP connection.
    The attribute timerGuard is not applicable for APS connection and 54xx NEs.
    The attributes timerDetectionGuard and timerRecoveryGuard are not applicable for SNCP connections.

    autoReversionType timeOfDay parameters:

    Parameter Value

    todrTime

    <start time for TODR>

    todrTimePeriod

    <between 5 mins and 5 hrs>

    todrHoldbackEnabled

    <boolean value>

    todrHoldbackPeriod

    <between 5 mins and 72 hrs>

  1. Retrieve the relationship between Façade and Service Intent.

    Description: Every facade from a client is mapped to a Service Intent on the Navigator MC server. This call will provide the target id which is the service Intent ID of the desired service and will be used in the subsequent calls to the Navigator MC server.

    The response will contain multiple entries. The user needs to filter out the one based on the sourceId which is the facade id created in step 3.

    {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/relationships

    Sample response:

  {
      "id": "5f1657e1-d4fc-4ae2-afe9-a3334f65f937",
      "relationshipTypeId": "ifd.v6.relationshipTypes.FcHasFacade",
      "properties": {},
      "sourceId": "5f1657df-4084-4be5-9986-99e47cdd6540",
      "requirementName": "facades",
      "targetId": "5f1657e0-0635-48b5-a467-68c0a3f40e5d",
      "capabilityName": "l1NCPProtClientServiceIntentFacadeCapability",
      "orchState": "active",
      "reason": "",
      "providerData": {}
  }

  1. Commit route for L1 NCP SNCP service

    Description: Commit route store tpe and fre expectation of L1 NCP SNCP service in NSI.

    POST - {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/{INTENT_RSC_ID}/operations

POST - {BP_SERVER}/bpocore/market/api/v1/resources/5f1657e0-0635-48b5-a467-68c0a3f40e5d/operations

Step 5 request route data passes in commit route request service for NCP SNCP.

Sample request:

{
  "interface": "commitRoute",
  "inputs": {
    "routes": [
      {{SELECTED_ROUTE}}
    ],
    "routes_equipment":[
    ]
  }
}

    Request parameter:

  {
